description.summary: layer surface interactive move and resize integration for treeland

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a layer-shell client hand interactive move and resize over to the compositor: the client starts an operation with begin_resize or begin_move, the compositor drives the surface size or position through layer-surface configure events, and reports state, rejection reasons, and placement through this interface.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_layer_shell_extension_manager_v1

description.summary: manager for layer surface interactive move and resize

interface.description:
This interface allows a layer-shell client (typically a dock surface) to opt in to compositor-driven interactive move and resize, so the compositor owns the drag state machine and the client follows the resulting layer-surface configure events instead of racing its own set_size requests.
This protocol applies to any layer-shell surface. The compositor drives the surface's size (begin_resize) or position (begin_move) over an interactive drag; whether a particular axis is freely resizable depends on the concrete anchor configuration.

entry.name: layer_shell_extension_exists
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a layer shell extension object bound

entry.name: wl_surface_invalid
entry.summary: the get_layer_shell_extension_object wl_surface argument is invalid

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the layer shell extension manager

request.description: Destroy the manager object. This does not destroy layer shell objects created with get_layer_shell_extension_object; those remain valid until their wl_surface is destroyed or the client destroys them.

request.name: get_layer_shell_extension_object

description.summary: create a layer shell extension object for an existing wl_surface

request.description:
Create a layer shell extension object for an existing wl_surface. The surface is expected to be a layer-shell surface; the compositor reports layer_shell_extension_exists if the same wl_surface already has a layer shell extension object bound.
The layer shell extension object is tied to the wl_surface: when the wl_surface is destroyed, the treeland_layer_shell_extension_object_v1 object is destroyed by the compositor as well, and the client must call get_layer_shell_extension_object again for a new wl_surface. A layer shell extension object must not outlive its wl_surface.

interface.name: treeland_layer_shell_extension_object_v1

description.summary: compositor-driven interactive resize and move for a layer surface

interface.description:
The client starts an interactive resize with begin_resize, passing a serial from a recent pointer event. The compositor validates the serial, takes over the drag (like xdg_toplevel.resize) and drives the surface size through the standard layer-surface configure events, reporting the resize state and any size restrictions through this interface.
The client may also start an interactive move with begin_move; the exact move semantics and state reporting are not yet finalized.

enum.name: resize_edge
enum.description:
Values indicate which edge (or corner) of the surface is being dragged in a resize operation, named from the surface's own perspective. Values are bit flags matching xdg_toplevel.resize_edge exactly: 1=top, 2=bottom, 4=left, 8=right; corner values are the OR of two adjacent edges (top_left=5=1|4, bottom_left=6=2|4, top_right=9=1|8, bottom_right=10=2|8).
The layer surface is anchored to one screen edge and changes height, vertical surfaces (left/right) change width. Whether an edge may be dragged at all depends on the surface's anchor; see begin_resize.

enum.name: resize_error

description.summary: reason a begin_resize request was rejected

enum.description: begin_resize is rejected (no resize starts) when the serial is stale (bad_serial), the edges value is not a valid resize_edge (bad_edges), or the compositor cannot take over the resize right now (inactive). The compositor then emits resize_rejected with the reason; an accepted request instead emits resizing(1).

entry.name: bad_serial
entry.summary: serial does not match a recent pointer button press on the seat

entry.name: bad_edges
entry.summary: edges is not a valid resize_edge value

entry.name: inactive
entry.summary: the compositor cannot take over the resize right now (no container, surface not layer, animation running, or seat refused the takeover)

entry.name: bad_surface
entry.summary: the surface is invalid or has been destroyed

description.summary: destroy the layer shell extension object

request.name: begin_resize
request.description:
Start a compositor-driven interactive resize of the associated surface. The seat and serial must come from a recent pointer button press on that seat; an invalid serial makes the compositor reject the request with resize_error.bad_serial. edges names which edge (or corner) of the surface the client wants to drag, using the xdg_toplevel.resize_edge values. The client owns which edge it drags; the compositor executes the drag on the reported edge.
The compositor rejects the request with resize_error.bad_edges when any of the requested edges is anchored: an anchored edge is already fixed in place by the layer-shell layout, so dragging it has no effect. A corner value (top_left etc.) requires both of its edges to be unanchored, otherwise the request is rejected. A dock anchored to a single screen edge, for example, may only be dragged on the edge opposite to its anchor.
Any other value is rejected with resize_error.bad_edges. The compositor emits resizing(1) once the drag actually starts, resizing(0) when it ends, and drives the surface size through the standard layer-surface configure events. On a rejected request it emits resize_rejected with a resize_error reason; in that case no resize starts and resizing is never emitted for this request.
The min/max size arguments bound this resize only: they apply while this drag is active and are not a persistent property of the surface. A value of 0 means no limit in that direction (minimum 0 / maximum unbounded); negative values are treated as 0. The compositor clamps the target size to these limits and reflects the clamped size through the standard layer-surface configure event. Invalid limits (min > max with both non-zero) are ignored for that axis.

arg.name: seat
arg.summary: seat the resize is initiated from

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial of a recent pointer button press on seat

arg.name: edges
arg.summary: edge(s) the client wants to drag, none of which may be anchored

arg.name: min_width
arg.summary: minimum width for this resize, 0 for none

arg.name: min_height
arg.summary: minimum height for this resize, 0 for none

arg.name: max_width
arg.summary: maximum width for this resize, 0 for none

arg.name: max_height
arg.summary: maximum height for this resize, 0 for none

event.name: resizing
event.description: resizing=1 when the compositor starts the interactive drag, resizing=0 when it ends. The client may use this to run a settle / spring animation after the drag finishes. resizing(1) is only emitted after the compositor has actually taken over the drag; rejected begin_resize requests instead cause a resize_rejected event.

arg.name: resizing
arg.summary: 1 during interactive resize, 0 after it ends

event.name: resize_rejected
event.description: Emitted when a begin_resize request is rejected: the reason names a resize_error value. No resize starts and resizing is never emitted for the rejected request. The client should use this instead of inferring acceptance from the absence of a resizing(1) event, and may fall back to its own drag logic.
